fields.label: Correction status
fields.text: No correction/change-history listed on article page (2026-10-11).

fields.label: Precise theorem
fields.text: Lemma 1 (eq.1): ideal IQT1/IQT2 eps_unf=(1/2+1/(2 sqrt2))^N. Lemma 2 (eqs 2-3) robustness; Lemma 3 (eqs 4-5) correctness; Lemma 4 (eq 6) eps_priv=beta_E; Theorem 1 (eqs 7-10) realistic unforgeability eps_unf = exp(-Pnoqub N/3 (nu_unf/Pnoqub-1)^2) + exp(-N f(...)); Theorem 2 (eq 11) 2^M presentation points, eps_unf^M = C eps_unf (C = number of pairs of spacelike-separated presentation points). Exact transcriptions in THEOREM_REGISTRY_SEED.yaml.

fields.label: Input model
fields.text: Bob prepares N qubit (or >2-dim multi-photon) states; BB84 bases up to angle theta; preparation biases beta_PS, beta_PB; multi-photon probability Pnoqub; losses with Alice reporting Lambda; Table 5 imperfections; Table 6 assumptions A-G.

fields.label: Verifier model
fields.text: Two (2^M) presentation points; Bob's agent B_b validates locally if Hamming distance d(x_b,r_b) <= |Delta_b| gamma_err (QT1 step 12); abort if n < gamma_det N.

fields.label: Adversary capabilities
fields.text: Dishonest Alice: arbitrary quantum operations on received systems (only potential restriction via assumption G, phase randomisation). Dishonest Bob (privacy): side channels excluded by assumption E; detector symmetry assumption F.

fields.label: Tested parameters
fields.text: Experiment (QT1 quantum stage, M=1): mu=0.09, 10 MHz, N=4e7, eta=0.21, Pdet=0.019 (0.01856), E=0.058, beta_PB=2.4e-3, beta_PS=3.6e-3, Pnoqub=3.8e-3, theta<=10 deg (assumed). Fig.5 numerical example: eps_rob=eps_cor=eps_unf=1e-9, gamma_det=0.018, nu_unf=3.9e-3; beta_max=6e-6 at E=0.058,theta=10deg; ~2.3e-4 at theta=5deg,E=0.03. The experiment did NOT achieve guaranteed unforgeability.

fields.label: Proof dependencies
fields.text: Supplementary Notes II-VIII (Lemma 6, Lemma 7, Chernoff bounds, piling-up lemma); Lemma 5 extends Lemmas 1 & 12 of ref 53 (multi-photon attacks); flexible S-money of ref 28 (Kent & Pitalúa-García 2020, arXiv:1908.08143).

fields.label: Datasets
fields.text: No raw data deposit identified on article page (NOT_VERIFIED that none exists).

fields.label: License
fields.text: Article: CC BY 4.0 (stated on article page). SI PDF: same article licence assumed (NOT_VERIFIED separately). Patent: A. Kent, US 10,790,972 (competing-interests statement).

fields.label: Limitations
fields.text: Experiment covers quantum stage only; parameters insufficient for unforgeability; Table 6 assumptions are idealisations (authors say so); security does not rely on spacetime constraints but advantage over classical does; clock synchronisation left to future work.

fields.label: What QMint adds
fields.text: Nothing new theoretically. QMint can (a) reproduce Lemmas 2-3/Theorem 1 numerically and the Fig.5 region (L1), (b) use them as the S2 bound inside a parameter search with explicit Table 6 assumption flags. Parameter selection in Fig.5 is hand-tuned by the authors ('we do not claim our numerical example is optimal'); an optimiser over the SAME bounds is the only plausible increment.

related.title: H1 · Cross-protocol, game-typed certificate format
related.subtitle: Novelty hypothesis
related.summary: A machine-checkable certificate that ties every ε to a named game (W1, W1_CV, S1, S2, D1, …), a theorem ID with a source anchor, assumption flags (e.g. P03 Table 6 A–G), and an evidence kind.

related.title: H2 · Systematic optimisation over published bounds
related.subtitle: Novelty hypothesis
related.summary: Treat P03 Lemmas 2–3 + Thm 1 (and P04 eqs.(19)–(23), P05 Thm 1) as *fixed, cited* constraints and search the free parameters (γ_det, γ_err, ν_cor, ν_unf, N, δ_h, δ_d) to minimise resource cost at fixed ε. Report the gap against each paper's published tuple. *…
